doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: New Orleans scene today: schooled versus street musicians
summary: He complains New Orleans players are not progressing, split between college kids and street musicians.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: What’s New Orleans like as a jazz center now? Is it at all?

Well there’s a lot of stuff going on there. One of the main things I don’t like about the New Orleans thing is they’re not really like progressing musically. They’re playing little like B flat licks, you know, but they’re not really progressing like for playing changes, playing different keys and stuff like that. We don’t have enough kids trying to do that. We have the kids in the colleges who aren’t the street smart type of musicians, so they’re getting the education but they can’t play the street music. Then we have the street guys who don’t go to school so they’re not really playing like a real educated higher form of
music. So I’d like to see more people like in the middle between these two things then, separated so far.
